issues.body: `obsTruncationNote` validates `total` only through `obsNum`, which accepts any finite number. A tampered or future document with `lanes_total: 12.5` beside 12 rows renders `showing 12 of 12.5 lanes` and a `0.5 more` title. These fields are counts and the generator only emits non-negative integers; treating a malformed fractional value as authoritative violates the function's stated rule that an unreadable total draws nothing and produces an operator-facing lie. The hostile executed-page case covers strings, booleans, null, negatives, equal and smaller values, but omits a non-integral finite number, so it cannot catch this.
issues.fix_hint: Require `Number.isInteger(collected)` (and non-negativity) before rendering. Add a literal fractional total to the executed hostile-page fixture and assert that it produces no note.
issues.title: Fractional totals are trusted as row counts

issues.body: `obsHealthCard` explicitly supports and documents `shown === 0 && total > 0`, but `renderObservability` calls it only under `if (lanes.length)`. Thus a document with `lanes: []` and `lanes_total: 50` renders no `showing 0 of 50 lanes` note. The same gate also hides non-empty defer/exit slices or their truncation notes whenever lanes is empty. The page tests never supply a positive total with an empty corresponding slice, so the claimed hand-edited-data behavior is not actually tested.
issues.fix_hint: Render the health card when any health rows exist or any valid health total exceeds its shown length, and add an executed-page case with empty lanes plus a positive lane total (and preferably defer/exit data) that asserts the literal note and preserved sibling content.
issues.title: The lane gate makes the promised zero-row truncation note unreachable

verdict.summary: The validated-row totals and normal over/under-cap tests are thoughtfully wired, but the browser does not fully enforce the count contract it presents. It accepts non-integral numbers as totals and can therefore render a fabricated fractional row count, contrary to the stated fail-closed handling of unusable/tampered totals. In addition, the health renderer is never invoked when the lane slice is empty, so its documented and intentionally implemented `showing 0 of N` behavior cannot occur for lanes (and defer/exit information can be suppressed by the lane gate). The current executed tests omit both controls.
